question: does a nonlinear Random Forest on exactly Ridge's 24 features beat the direct Ridge model?

constant_shift_feature_sanity.sample: first train examples in file order (train only)

cv_protocol.method: GroupKFold(5) by song over all train examples (all five variants of a note share its song, so siblings never straddle a fold)

full24.rule: among candidates within tolerance of the best mean CV MAE: larger min_samples_leaf, then smaller max_depth (None = unlimited), then fewer features per split, then lower CV MAE

center4.rule: among candidates within tolerance of the best mean CV MAE: larger min_samples_leaf, then smaller max_depth (None = unlimited), then fewer features per split, then lower CV MAE

train_in_sample.note: in-sample on the fitted rows; optimistic for a forest

validation.post_hoc_only: all breakdowns computed after the model was fixed

feature_importance.permutation_method: sklearn permutation_importance on validation, MAE, 5 repeats; interpretation only
feature_importance.caveat: the four center features (and the percentiles) are strongly correlated; a forest splits credit among correlated features, and permuting one leaves its correlates intact, so individual importances understate the group and should not be read as unique contributions
